LinkedIn post by the Founder of Popcorn | Restaurant technology marketing (23h, edited)

I read the Wall Street Journal piece on big QSR walking back their kiosk experiments, so I decided to run my own (tiny) test at a local Wendy's.

Pretty decent in-store traffic. Couple of moms and their kids and a scattering of retirees. I joined a bank of two huge kiosks. I took one, and an older couple was already working through the other — husband driving the screen, wife watching over his shoulder.

I ordered a Double Bacon Classic combo, built a five part custom Diet Coke at a beautiful Coke Freestyle machine, and was unwrapping my burger before they finished. I FELT SO BAD just watching this instead of stepping in, truly. But it confirmed exactly what the article was saying — and kinda what most of us already knew.

Turns out now McDonald's is retraining over two million workers worldwide and now grades franchisees partly on hospitality. Burger King has started requiring counters to stay staffed and is moving kiosks off to the side in new locations. Wendy's is even reviewing its own AI drive-thru pilots to see if they're actually helping anyone (which I personally really like). And Starbucks is putting lots of fresh money into training, too.

McDonald's global chief people officer told WSJ that price and food still matter, but experience has become a bigger deal than it used to be. That's a pretty big admission.

“They want a friendly face,” BK CEO, Curtis said of the chain's new restaurants. “We have to lean in to that because that's evaporating in the fast food space.” Praise be.

First, I don't think the tech is a mistake! Kiosks do amazing things with maxing tickets and collecting incredible data. But there's a real lesson here about where technology should be doing the work and where a person needs to be standing at the counter. #frictionisbad

I'm recording a new Modern Solutions for Modern Restaurants podcast this morning, breaking down what's actually happening across the industry and what it means if you're building or buying ordering tech right now. I'll make sure to revisit this post and pop the link in the comments.

Would love to hear your stories...

PS: best Freestyle recipe: 1/2 Diet Coke, 1/4 Cherry, 1/8 Vanilla, 1/8 Lime — thank me later.
